title: THREAT Matrix Experimental Scoring Overlay Schema
description: JSON Schema for docs/data/scoring-overlay.json and for scored case records. The overlay is experimental, opt-in, and non-normative: it attaches authored, type-level estimates to indicator classes of the THREAT Matrix vocabulary (framework.json). The values have not been validated against outcomes, do not predict violence, are never a score of a person, and must not be used as grounds for adverse action. The vocabulary is complete without this document. The root of this schema describes the overlay document; $defs.scored_case_record describes one scored case record and $defs.instance_assessment its instance factors. Every object is closed. Rules that need both documents (the key set of indicator_scores equals the indicator IDs of framework.json, the stored weight equals the composite of its axes, the band follows from the stored weight and the floor, a record quotes the authored band) are enforced by scripts/lint/validate.py with --overlay and --records.

applies_to_framework_version.description: The framework.json content version whose indicator and tactic IDs this overlay keys on. scripts/lint/validate.py requires it to equal the version of the framework document it is checked against.

normative.description: The overlay is not part of the vocabulary's contract. A consumer may ignore it entirely.

validation_status.description: The values have not been validated. This is a constant in this schema version: a claim of validation needs a schema change that adds a reference to the published study.

scope.description: Every value describes a class of behavior, never a case, a person, or an incident.

not_a_risk_score.description: The values are not a risk score for any individual.

notice.description: The limitation notice a consumer must keep with any use of the overlay.

rubric.description: How type_weight is derived from the four axes and mapped to a type band. Reference material for a consumer that recomputes or overrides the values.

composite_math.description: The formula for type_weight: the fourth root of impact_potential times blast_radius_potential times recoverability_inverse times (10 minus detectability), rounded to two decimals.

type_band_thresholds.description: Lower bound of each band on the stored two-decimal type_weight. scripts/lint/validate.py requires low to be 0 and the four values to be strictly increasing.

type_band_floor_rule.description: The floor rule: which behavior classes carry a type_band_floor that holds the type band at or above a stated value whatever the computed weight.

floored_indicators.description: The complete list of indicators that carry a type_band_floor. scripts/lint/validate.py requires the set of score entries with a type_band_floor to equal this list exactly, so a floor cannot be added or removed without changing the published rule.

detectability_guidance.description: Reading guidance for the detectability axis.

blast_radius_guidance.description: Reading guidance and method base rates for the blast_radius_potential axis.

method_collateral_base_rates.description: Per-method base rates on the 0 to 10 axis scale. note is prose; every other key is a bounded number.

axis_confidence_rubric.description: Level meanings and the derivation rule for axis_confidence. The rule is mechanical and scripts/lint/validate.py recomputes it for every indicator.

rubric_version.description: Version of the rubric. Changes when the formula, thresholds, or guidance change.

calibration_guidance.description: Guidance for a consumer that moves the thresholds for its own environment.

instance_conditioning.description: The instance-conditioning layer of the overlay: how a type band is joined to a case record's instance factors to give a conditioned priority. Escalate-only: the join may raise priority above the type band and never lowers it.

factors.description: The six instance factors, each exactly once. These are the required properties of $defs.instance_assessment.

tactic_priorities.description: Type-level priority class per tactic, keyed by tactic ID. Characterizes the typical urgency of the tactic class, never the urgency of a case. scripts/lint/validate.py requires exactly one entry for every tactic of framework.json: none missing, none extra.

indicator_scores.description: Type-level scores keyed by indicator ID. scripts/lint/validate.py requires the key set to equal the indicator IDs of framework.json: none missing, none extra.

prose.description: A non-empty text value with no leading or trailing whitespace.

tactic_id.description: Tactic ID, same grammar as framework.schema.json.

indicator_id.description: Indicator ID, same grammar as framework.schema.json.

score_number.description: A number on the 0 to 10 scale. scripts/lint/validate.py also rejects NaN and Infinity, which JSON does not allow.

band.description: A band, in rising order: low, medium, high, critical.

confidence_level.description: Evidence basis of one axis value. Categorical only. A thin axis is a wider error bar and a reason for earlier human review; it never lowers a band.

indicator_score.description: The experimental type-level score of one indicator class. Every part is required; a score with a missing axis, weight, or band is invalid.

axes.description: The four authored axis values, each on the 0 to 10 scale and recorded to one decimal place (the decimal rule is checked by scripts/lint/validate.py).

impact_potential.description: Magnitude of harm the behavior class directly produces or imminently enables.

blast_radius_potential.description: Geographic or population scope of the harm if it lands.

recoverability_inverse.description: How hard the harm the behavior class directly produces is to undo. Higher is less recoverable.

detectability.description: How observable the behavior class is while in progress. Enters the composite as 10 minus this value.

type_weight.description: The composite of the four axes per rubric.composite_math, stored to two decimals. scripts/lint/validate.py recomputes it with a tolerance of 0.005.

type_band.description: The band of the stored type_weight per rubric.type_band_thresholds, raised to type_band_floor when a floor is present.

type_band_floor.description: Optional floor. When present, type_band is never below it; type_weight is left as computed.

axis_confidence.description: Evidence basis of each axis value, derived by the rule in rubric.axis_confidence_rubric.

instance_assessment.description: The instance factors of one case: discrete observations about a specific situation, kept separate from the type-level values. The same six factors and values as instance_factors in the score-free case record (case-record.schema.json). The overlay ships no instances; a consumer writes one per case.

target_focus.description: Direction of the observed behavior toward a target: diffuse (no resolved target), narrowing (a candidate set or associated place), specific_target (a specific subject or asset). unknown when not assessable.

pathway_stage.description: Assessed position on the pathway to violence in this case, which may lead or lag the indicator class's type-level phase.

means_in_hand.description: Whether the means are actually held now. Possession, not eligibility: lawful ability to acquire is not means in hand. unknown is the default and never lowers priority.

tempo_trajectory.description: Direction and rate of movement along the pathway across observations.

proximity_access.description: Access state relative to the target. A state, not a stage: an insider has access without ever breaching. unknown is the default and never lowers priority.

source_credibility.description: Reliability of the reporting behind the record. It conditions how much the other five factors can raise priority and never lowers the type band.

basis.description: Optional free-text evidentiary basis or assessor note.

scored_case_record.description: An experimental scored case record: one indicator's type band joined to the instance factors of a case. Escalate-only: conditioned_priority may sit above type_band and never below it, which the conditionals on this object enforce. Whether the instance held or raised the band is not stored; it is read by comparing the two fields. Leaving a queue is a disposition, never a lowered priority. Band fidelity cannot be expressed in a schema: scripts/lint/validate.py --overlay ... --records ... requires indicator_id to exist in framework.json and type_band to equal the overlay's authored type_band for that indicator, so the escalate-only rule cannot be defeated by misquoting the band. The default record for case work is the score-free case record (case-record.schema.json); this record is for consumers who have opted in to the overlay.

indicator_id.description: The indicator whose type band is being conditioned. Must exist in framework.json.

type_band.description: The overlay's authored type_band for indicator_id, quoted exactly. This is the floor: conditioned_priority is never below it.

conditioned_priority.description: The resulting triage priority, at or above type_band.

framework_version.description: Optional. The framework.json content version the record was written against. When present, scripts/lint/validate.py requires it to equal the version of the framework document being checked.

overlay_version.description: Optional. The overlay version whose type_band the record quotes. When present, scripts/lint/validate.py requires it to equal the overlay_version of the overlay being checked.

primary_objective_evidence_tier.description: Optional. How well the primary objective behind the observed behavior, and so the matrix placement, is established in this case. stated: explicit. strongly_inferred and weakly_inferred: inferred from behavior. contested: the evidence conflicts, or whether there is a hostile actor at all is disputed. unknown: no basis for inference.

disposition.description: Optional case-management outcome, recorded beside the priority and never written back into it. Same values as the score-free case record.
